title: Jacob's ladder (Genesis 28:10–22)
hook: asleep on a stone, he dreams of angels going up and down
tomorrow: seven years like a few days

segments.voice: Yesterday: the stolen blessing, and Esau's cry, bless me, even me also. Your line was bless me too. Who got a blessing of their own from you? Day fifty-five.

Esau is furious. He says he'll kill his brother once their father dies. So Rebekah sends Jacob away, to her brother Laban, far to the north. And Jacob, the quiet one who stayed in the tents, is suddenly alone on the road with nothing. No family, no flocks, no plan. The sun goes down. In the old JPS translation: "And he lighted upon the place, and tarried there all night, because the sun was set." Not a town. Not an inn. Just the place, wherever he happened to be when it got dark. He takes some stones, puts them under his head, and lies down on the ground. Anyone who has spent a night in an airport, a hospital waiting room or a strange bed knows that place. Nowhere. And there, he dreams.
screen: `RUNNING FROM ESAU.` → `HE LIGHTED UPON THE PLACE.` → `A STONE FOR A PILLOW.`

segments.voice: "And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven; and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it." Notice the order: ascending, then descending. You'd expect angels to come down from heaven first. Rashi, the medieval commentator, has a beautiful answer. The angels who had guarded Jacob in his home country were going up, their shift over, and new angels, for the road ahead, were coming down. A changing of the guard over a sleeping man. Then God stands beside him and promises: the land, children like the dust of the earth, and "I am with thee, and will keep thee whithersoever thou goest." Jacob wakes up and says the sentence that gives today its line: "Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not." He was sure he was nowhere. He was at the gate of heaven. He names the spot Beth-el, the house of God. Here's a small word with a big afterlife: the place. In later Hebrew, HaMakom, the Place, becomes one of the names for God. A midrash explains: God is the place of the world, and the world is not God's place. And the Talmud says that Jacob, lighting on the place at nightfall, began the evening prayer. So now all three: Abraham the morning, Isaac the afternoon, Jacob the night. Jacob prayed in the dark, on a stone, in the middle of nowhere, and found out that nowhere had God in it all along.
screen: `A LADDER FROM EARTH TO HEAVEN.` · `UP FIRST: A CHANGE OF GUARD.` · `I KNEW IT NOT.` · `HAMAKOM — THE PLACE.` · then, large: `SURELY THE LORD IS IN THIS PLACE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice. Settle, and breathe. Notice exactly where you are right now. Not where you wish you were. This room, this car, this bench, this bed. Look at one ordinary thing in it: a wall, a cup, a patch of floor. Let your breath slow. Then, silently, say Jacob's words, or your own version of them: this place is holy, and I didn't know it. You don't have to feel anything special. Just let the ordinary place be enough. The bell holds the time.
Jacob's ladder. A dream on a stone in the middle of nowhere: angels going up and down, and God standing beside him.
Your line: God was here all along. Today, stop in one ordinary place, a kitchen, a bus stop, a hallway, and call it holy. Day fifty-five.

screen: `DAY 55 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: SEVEN YEARS LIKE A FEW DAYS.`

howItsDone: Jews read Jacob's dream in the Torah portion Vayetze; tradition credits Jacob with the evening prayer, Maariv, and many Jews use HaMakom, the Place, as a name for God, as in the words said to comfort mourners.

fork.setup: you're Jacob, alone, running from your brother. the sun has set and there's no town. what do you do?
options: lie down right there with a stone under your head.
fork.reveal: he lights upon the place, sleeps on the ground, and dreams of a ladder to heaven. he wakes and says, I knew it not.

original.note: Hebrew: a ladder or stairway. the word appears only here in the Bible.

trapdoor: what you thought: a dream about a ladder to heaven.
what it means: a man on the run discovers that the middle of nowhere was the gate of heaven: God was here all along.
what a scholar hears: HaMakom, the Place, as a name for God (Genesis Rabbah 68:9), and Berakhot 26b reading vayifga bamakom as Jacob's evening prayer.

notes: Confirm JPS 1917 wording of Genesis 28:11, 28:12, 28:15 and 28:16.
The carry is lowercase 'god' in the index; the script's voice capitalizes God. Suggest capitalizing the index carry (owner-approved edit).
Rashi on 28:12: angels of the land ascend, angels outside the land descend. Confirm.
Genesis Rabbah 68:9: God is the place of the world, and the world is not His place. Confirm.
Sulam appears only here in the Hebrew Bible: confirm (hapax legomenon).
howItsDone: HaMakom in the mourners' comfort formula (HaMakom yenachem). Confirm.
